title: In a market entry case, agree the goal and time frame, then test attractiveness, winnability and payback
description: The first question to ask in a market entry case, how to structure it, and the trap to avoid.
hook: Market entry cases ask a yes or no question: should the client go in? Here is how to get to a clear answer.
body:
The first question to ask

What is the goal, and over what time frame?

How to build your structure

  • Is the market attractive? (size and growth, margins, barriers to entry)
  • Can we win? (competitors, customer needs, our edge)
  • Will it pay? (revenue, costs, upfront investment, payback)
  • Can we pull it off? (capabilities we lack, build / partner / buy, timing and pilot, risks)

The trap most people fall into

Forgetting entry mode and timing; no pilot.

For the full tree, with every branch, read the market entry framework.

Two prompts to try

Should a luxury hotel group launch a budget hotel brand?

Show a model structure
  • Market: Size and growth of budget hotels; Competitors and their returns
  • Economics: Cost to build or convert, room rates, occupancy; Return vs our cost of capital
  • Fit and risk: Can we run low-cost hotels well?; Damage to the luxury brand
  • Cannibalisation: Guests who would trade down from our hotels; Net new profit

Where to start: Economics per hotel: if a single hotel doesn't make money, nothing else matters.

The trap: Forgetting the brand risk and cannibalisation for an existing luxury group.

Should an airline launch a co-branded credit card?

Show a model structure
  • Customer value: Who would use it; Points earned and redeemed
  • Economics: Bank pays us per card and per point; Cost of rewards (seats) and marketing
  • Partner: Which bank, terms, exclusivity; Risk sharing
  • Risks: Brand if the bank treats customers badly; Too many free seats given away

Where to start: Economics: what the bank pays per point vs what a reward seat costs us.

The trap: Treating it as a pure brand decision when it is mainly a points business.
outro: Small things like this add up. Try it in your next practice case and notice how it changes the conversation. Practise this case type in the free casebook: every case has a worked answer.
